record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Computation as Questions about Two-Way Deterministic Pushdown Automaton Languages
record.original_question: Is every language decidable by a nondeterministic Turing machine in linear time, that is every language in NTIME(n), also decidable in deterministic polynomial time, so that NTIME(n) is a subset of P-TIME?

evidence.quote: In [2] this question is reduced to the questions: "IsP-TIME closed under nonerasing homomorphism ?" and "Is N TIME(n) ~_ P- TIME ?"

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let NTIME(n) denote the class of languages L ⊆ {0,1}* such that there exists a nondeterministic multitape Turing machine M and a constant c > 0 with the following property: for every input x, M halts on every computation branch within c·|x| steps, and M has at least one accepting computation on input x if and only if x ∈ L. Let P (deterministic polynomial time) denote the class of languages decidable by a deterministic Turing machine in time O(|x|^k) for some fixed integer k ≥ 1.

Determine whether the inclusion
    NTIME(n) ⊆ P
holds. Equivalently: is it the case that every language accepted by some nondeterministic Turing machine in linear time can also be decided by some deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether NTIME(n) ⊆ P is a long-standing open problem in computational complexity theory. It is a special case (and weaker form) of the P vs NP problem: since NP = ⋃_c NTIME(n^c), a positive answer to NTIME(n) ⊆ P would not immediately collapse NP to P, but no proof of either NTIME(n) ⊆ P or NTIME(n) ⊄ P is known. No source indicates a resolution.

status_evidence.title: NTIME - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: NTIME(f(n)) is the set of decision problems decidable by a nondeterministic Turing machine running in time O(f(n)); NP = union over c of NTIME(n^c).
status_evidence.claim: NTIME(n) is a well-defined class and its relationship to deterministic polynomial time is part of the broader open P vs NP question.

status_evidence.title: P versus NP problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Whether P equals NP is a major open problem in computer science.
status_evidence.claim: The general containment of nondeterministic polynomial time in P is unresolved, and the linear-time subcase NTIME(n) ⊆ P is likewise not known.
